study: The operator's %R trend trade, as one complete rule (operator 2026-10-24): buy when the fast and slow %R lines are both rising out of the bottom (oversold) zone; no opens while %R is sideways; sell when the lines turn down.
registered_at: 2026-10-24, before any script, feature or outcome
origin: Operator 10/24: 'Sideways is the zone between the top and bottom levels. We want to buy when %R is trending from the bottom level (oversold) to the top level (overbought); the fast and slow lines support a profit trend as they move up. When not trending upward, no open, unless at the very top with open squares (risky). When trending down, we should be looking to sell.' Prompted by the CCI 10/23 review: the live pre-square arm bought at the TOPS of relief bounces.
prior: LOW (~10%): entries alone were tested and matched random minutes - leaving oversold (10/15, lift -4 / +1 bp), both lines turning up (10/17, 283k onsets ~0), slow-line rising filter (10/16, halves reversed). New here: the complete trade with a %R EXIT, which no earlier test used.
lines: The desk's exact definitions (signals.py, live config): FAST = Williams %R(21) smoothed by EMA(span 7); SLOW = %R(112) smoothed by EMA(span 3); both on the 1-minute grid. BOTTOM ZONE = both lines <= -80 (rte_threshold 20); TOP ZONE = both >= -20; SQUARE = top zone with |fast - slow| <= 15 (rte_confluence_max).
data: Warehouse SIP 1-minute RTH bars, the full universe each day (~1,640-1,950 liquid names, >= $10, >= $20M ADV, active + inactive), sessions 2026-05-11 .. 10-15 (halves A <= 07-29 < B). The lines are computed on the name's RTH minutes with its previous warehouse session prepended for warm-up (>= 112 bars before 09:45 needed; a name without its previous session that day is skipped and counted). Declared: the live desk computes %R on IEX bars; SIP here.

rule.oversold_event: a minute at which BOTH lines are <= -80.
rule.entry_signal: at the close of minute t (09:45 .. 15:00): an oversold event occurred within t-20 .. t, AND fast(t) > -80 (it has left the bottom zone), AND both lines are RISING: fast(t) - fast(t-5) >= 5 points and slow(t) - slow(t-5) > 0.
rule.no_sideways: implied: a minute where either line is not rising is not an entry; there is no other entry path in the primary (the 'very top with open squares' case is information only).
rule.entry: the open of minute t+1 for the FIRST qualifying minute t; no price filter at entry (the only floor is universe membership: prior-day RAW close >= $10).
rule.exit_signal: at the close of minute u > entry minute: the fast line is falling: fast(u) < fast(u-3) ('turns down').
rule.exit: the open of minute u+1; or the close of the last bar at or before 15:59 if no exit signal by then.
rule.reentry: one open trade per name; after an exit a new entry needs a NEW oversold event after the exit minute.

controls.d_same_name: a seeded random entry minute in (entry minute, entry minute + 60] on the same name-day (seed sha256(sym|day|entry|'wrtrend-d')), held for the SAME number of minutes as the trade (or to 15:59). Declared bias: later-minute controls run about +1 bp in the trade's favour on this universe (10/22 placebo finding).
controls.x_cross_name: a seeded random OTHER warehouse name the same day with bars at the trade's entry and exit minutes (seed 'wrtrend-x'), same entry and exit minutes.
controls.power_controls: second draws (seeds 'wrtrend-d2', 'wrtrend-x2') for the MDE only.

statistic: Per half, per day: mean over that day's trades of (trade - d control) and (trade - x control); day-equal; day-clustered t.
pass: In BOTH halves: (trade - d) >= +5 bp with t >= 2.0 AND (trade - x) >= +5 bp with t >= 2.0 AND mean trade net (after 5 bp) > 0 AND dropping the 3 best days keeps both lifts >= 0.
fail: t <= -2 on either lift in a half, or both halves' 97.5% upper bounds of BOTH lifts < +5 bp. Otherwise UNDERPOWERED.
power: Outcome-blind count step: trades and days per half; MDE = (2.0 + 0.84) x SD(day mean of control - control2) / sqrt(days) for d and x; floors >= 300 trades and >= 20 days per half and MDE <= 5 bp, else UNDERPOWERED with no outcome read; --score refuses unless both halves meet them.
information_only: exit when BOTH lines turn down (fast(u) < fast(u-3) and slow(u) < slow(u-3))
the 'very top with open squares' entries the operator called risky: a square with both lines rising, same exit
entries whose oversold event was a square-free bottom vs not
the desk's own exits (trail) instead of the %R exit, via a 15-minute time stop proxy
confirmation: A PASS is re-run unchanged on warehouse_confirm (2026-01-14 .. 04-24, never read), then a forward paper prereg; never a desk change by itself.
no_retuning: Lines, levels, the 20-minute oversold window, the 5-minute / 5-point rising rule, the 3-minute turn-down exit, entry window, cost, halves and floors are fixed.

amended.when: 2026-10-24, after result-skeptic round 1 FIX FIRST and the operator's answers, before any script or data.

operator_answers.sideways: 'not rising': any minute where either line is not climbing is sideways - no buy, wherever the lines sit (as registered).
operator_answers.open_squares: the FULL square: both lines >= -20 AND within 15 points (rte_tight); the risky top buy (information) uses it.
operator_answers.exit: any downturn (as registered): the first u >= t+1 with fast(u) < fast(u-3).

changes: (1a) Entry at the FIRST qualifying minute t; the exit scan starts at u = t+1 (a 1-minute minimum hold is possible).
(1b) Re-entry needs a new oversold event at a minute >= u+1 (after the exit fill).
(1d) Information exit: hold until the fast line turns down while in the top zone (>= -20) or falls back to <= -80.

(2) LINES: computed on a minute grid with grid fill (gaps <= 15 minutes filled flat at the previous close, as signals._minute_grid_pr); the overnight gap is not filled; warm-up from the previous warehouse session. A missing t+1 bar skips the trade (counted); a missing u+1 bar exits at the last close at or before u+1 (C2). Previous-close vs open jumps > 30% are counted and the name-day skipped (split mismatch).
(3) FEED: PRIMARY lines are computed on the warehouse IEX bars (what the live desk sees); all prices (entries, exits, controls) are SIP. The SIP-line run is information.

(4) CONTROLS: the x control needs only its entry bar; its exit uses C2. A control whose entry minute has no bar is redrawn with the next seed (counted, max 10). Information control d_rule_exit: the same random later minute, exited by the same %R rule.
(5) The count step also prints the hold-length distribution (median, share <= 3 minutes).
(6) Information: a 5-minute minimum hold before the exit rule applies. Declared risk: 1-3 minute holds are dominated by bar noise and the 5 bp cost.

(7) FAIL if EITHER lift's 97.5% upper bound < +5 bp in both halves, or the net's upper bound < 0 in both halves, or t <= -2 on either lift in a half; PASS also needs drop-top-5-names keeping both lifts >= 0; C4: missing warehouse names are counted against each day's manifest.
(8) The 'square-free bottom' cell uses os_tri (both <= -80 within 15 points); the '15-minute time stop' cell is renamed (not the desk trail).
(9) Family: the fourth %R entry-family test on this warehouse; a Bonferroni (t >= 2.73) reading is printed as information.
